 Humana and UnitedHealthcare Drew 58% of Early Medicare Advantage Applications Despite 2027 Cuts
 Published Nov 15, 2026 11:44 PM EST 
 By
 Elena Vega 
 Spencer Platt | Getty Images 
 Share on Twitter 
 Share on Facebook 
 Share on WhatsApp 
 Humana and UnitedHealthcare accounted for 58% of early Medicare Advantage applications submitted through brokerage firm Spark Advisors, with each insurer drawing nearly 30%, according to data covering Oct. 15 through Nov. 6 reported by Healthcare Finance News . The two insurers led sign-ups even as both cut plans for 2027.
 Part of Humana's activity came from its own members. Some clients whose Humana plans were discontinued chose another Humana plan, and Humana's plan cancellations affected more Spark clients than those of any other insurer.
 The pattern reflects a common choice in a disrupted year. When a plan ends, many seniors look first at another plan from a company they already know, hoping to keep the same doctors, pharmacy, and member services. With open enrollment ending Dec. 7, that instinct can save time, but it can also mean missing a better fit.
 Familiar Names Led Early Sign-Ups
 UnitedHealthcare led Spark applications for both kinds of special needs plans, accounting for 47% of applications for plans serving people with qualifying chronic conditions and 45% for plans serving people eligible for both Medicare and Medicaid. The insurer has made both plan types a priority for 2027. These plans are built for people with specific chronic illnesses or limited incomes, and they often coordinate care and extra benefits for those groups.
 "The days of one carrier being the default answer for every client are over," Spark CEO James Jiang said in the report.
 Humana has said early enrollment is running ahead of plan. "So far, AEP performance is ahead of our initial expectations," CEO Jim Rechtin said on the company's third-quarter earnings call, Insurance Business reported . AEP refers to the annual enrollment period. Rechtin added that Humana currently expects its membership to rise in 2027.
 Plan Exits Sent Seniors Back to Their Insurers
 The early numbers follow one of the most disruptive plan seasons in years. About 4.3 million Medicare beneficiaries will have a Medicare Advantage or standalone drug plan terminated at the end of 2026, according to KFF , including about 2.8 million people in Medicare Advantage drug plans open to general enrollment.
 Humana is ending plans that cover about 600,000 members, while about 390,000 UnitedHealthcare members are in plans being discontinued, Newsweek reported . Overall, UnitedHealthcare is cutting about 690 plans and Humana about 2,400 for 2027, according to a Healthcare Dive analysis of federal plan data.
 Staying with the same company does not mean keeping the same costs. In that analysis, UnitedHealthcare raised its maximum out-of-pocket limit 11% and its Part D deductible 33% for 2027, while Humana raised them by 8% and 30%. UnitedHealthcare's premiums rose 9%, compared with 1% for Humana. Healthcare Dive also cited CMS data showing that about 8 in 10 Medicare Advantage enrollees can stay in their current plan with the same or a lower premium.
 Some members are being moved without asking. KFF found about 500,000 enrollees in general plans and about 900,000 in special needs plans will be shifted automatically to another plan from the same insurer because of plan consolidations. Those members can still choose a different plan during open enrollment.
 Broker pay also shapes which plans seniors hear about, a factor many shoppers never see. Several insurers have stopped paying commissions on certain plans, which can make agents less likely to offer them. MedicalDaily previously reported that Aetna stopped paying brokers on 123 Medicare Advantage plans in 33 states for 2027.
 Limits of One Brokerage's Numbers
 The data reflect only applications submitted through Spark's network of agents. They do not include people who enrolled directly with an insurer, through Medicare's website or phone line, or through other brokers. Applications are also not the same as final enrollments, and early-season patterns can shift before the deadline. Because insurers' commission policies affect which plans brokers present, broker-network data may also differ from overall enrollment.
 The figures should not be read as national market share. They offer an early look at how broker-assisted shoppers are responding to plan exits, not a full count. Federal enrollment data covering the whole market will not be available until early next year.
 Deadlines and Checks Before December 7
 Medicare open enrollment runs through Dec. 7, with new coverage starting Jan. 1. People whose plans are ending also have a special enrollment period from Dec. 8, 2026, through Feb. 28, 2027. Those who do not pick a new plan generally return to Original Medicare and may need to add separate drug coverage.
 Before choosing a replacement, seniors can list every doctor, hospital, and prescription, then check each against the new plan's network and drug list using Medicare's Plan Finder . Comparing the out-of-pocket maximum, specialist copays, and prior authorization rules matters more than the premium alone, especially for people with chronic conditions.
 People leaving a terminated Medicare Advantage plan have a guaranteed right to buy certain Medigap policies without being denied or charged more for a pre-existing condition, according to KFF. That protection does not extend to members who were moved automatically into a consolidated plan. Free, unbiased help is available from State Health Insurance Assistance Programs, whose counselors do not earn commissions.
 Older adults managing heart failure, diabetes, cancer treatment, or dialysis face the highest stakes, because a network or drug-list change can interrupt care. Caregivers can help by gathering the plan's termination notice, current prescription list, and recent bills before calling a counselor.
 Open enrollment also brings scams . Seniors should be wary of unsolicited calls or texts offering plan changes or asking for a Medicare number, and should confirm any offer through Medicare or a trusted counselor before sharing personal information.
 MedicalDaily will report on final enrollment figures and any midseason plan changes as insurers and federal officials release them.

 Key Questions Answered
 What did the Spark Advisors data show? Humana and UnitedHealthcare drew 58% of early Medicare Advantage applications in Spark's broker network from Oct. 15 to Nov. 6, each with nearly 30%.
 Why are seniors choosing these insurers after plan cuts? Many are switching to another plan from the same company. Some Humana applications came from members whose current Humana plan was discontinued.
 Is this national market share? No. The data cover one brokerage's applications and exclude direct, online, and other broker enrollments.
 How many people are losing plans for 2027? About 4.3 million Medicare beneficiaries will have a Medicare Advantage or standalone drug plan terminated at the end of 2026, according to KFF.
 What is the deadline to choose a plan? Open enrollment ends Dec. 7. People whose plans are ending also have a special enrollment period through Feb. 28, 2027.
 Where can seniors get unbiased help? State Health Insurance Assistance Programs offer free counseling, and Medicare's Plan Finder compares networks and drug costs.
